<p>A <b>strider</b> is a <a href="/w/Passive_mob" class="mw-redirect" title="Passive mob">passive mob</a> found in <a href="/w/The_Nether" title="The Nether">the Nether</a>. It can walk on <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a> and be <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddled</a> by the <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a>, being directed via a <a href="/w/Warped_fungus_on_a_stick" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus on a stick">warped fungus on a stick</a>. They can be fed <a href="/w/Warped_fungus" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus">warped fungus</a> to breed, and are a source of <a href="/w/String" title="String">string</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Spawning">Spawning</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Strider?section=1&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Spawning" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Strider?action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section's source code: Spawning"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Striders can spawn in every <a href="/w/Nether" class="mw-redirect" title="Nether">Nether</a> biome. Groups of 2 to 4 striders spawn on spaces of <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a> that have an <a href="/w/Air" title="Air">air</a> block above. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, striders are the only <a href="/w/Passive_mob" class="mw-redirect" title="Passive mob">passive mob</a> in the Nether, so spawning attempts are made every 400 <a href="/w/Game_tick" class="mw-redirect" title="Game tick">game ticks</a>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, striders share the animal population cap with <a href="/w/Hoglin" title="Hoglin">hoglins</a>, and their spawn rate depends on the biome, being impacted by the ability of other mobs to spawn at a given coordinate.
</p><p>For every strider that spawns, there is a 1 in 10 chance for an additional <a href="/w/Baby" title="Baby">baby</a> strider to spawn riding on top of the spawned strider, as a <a href="/w/Baby_strider_jockey" class="mw-redirect" title="Baby strider jockey">baby strider jockey</a>. This behavior is limited to one strider.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The baby strider on the adult strider continues to grow, although it does not dismount the adult strider once it has grown up. 
</p><p>In <i><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a></i><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, adult striders also have a 1 in 30 chance of spawning being <a href="/w/Riding" title="Riding">ridden</a> by a <a href="/w/Zombified_piglin" class="mw-redirect" title="Zombified piglin">zombified piglin</a>, forming a <a href="/w/Strider_jockey" class="mw-redirect" title="Strider jockey">strider jockey</a>. When this happens, the strider spawns with a <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddle</a> and the zombified piglin spawns wielding a <a href="/w/Warped_fungus_on_a_stick" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus on a stick">warped fungus on a stick</a> instead of a <a href="/w/Golden_sword" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden sword">golden sword</a> or <a href="/w/Golden_spear" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden spear">spear</a>. The zombified piglin does not despawn naturally and does not count toward the mob cap. On <a href="/w/Peaceful" class="mw-redirect" title="Peaceful">Peaceful</a> difficulty, the zombified piglin despawns immediately, leaving a saddled strider.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>If a strider spawns under <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a>, it rises out of the <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a>. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, baby striders spawn more commonly than adult striders do, including when spawned by a spawn egg.
</p>

</li>
</ol></div></div>
<p>Striders wearing a saddle always drop the saddle upon death, regardless of if they spawn wearing it or if a player puts it on them. The saddle can be removed by using <a href="/w/Shears" title="Shears">shears</a> on the strider. 
When an adult strider is killed by a player or tamed <a href="/w/Wolf" title="Wolf">wolf</a>, <span class="animated"><span class="pixel-image animated-active xp-2" style="background-position:left center;background-size:16px 16px;padding-left:19px;background-repeat:no-repeat"></span><span class="pixel-image xp-6" style="background-position:left center;background-size:16px 16px;padding-left:19px;background-repeat:no-repeat"></span></span>1–3<span class="hidden-alt-text">XP</span> experience is dropped. Killing a baby strider yields no items or experience.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Behavior">Behavior</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Strider?section=4&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Behavior" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Strider?action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section's source code: Behavior"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">Lava</a> does not damage striders, and they can walk on top of it without sinking.
</p><p>Upon being harmed by another mob, striders attempt to flee for a few seconds while making "retreat" noises.
</p><p>Striders are damaged by <a href="/w/Water" title="Water">water</a>, <a href="/w/Rain" title="Rain">rain</a>, and <a href="/w/Splash_water_bottle" class="mw-redirect" title="Splash water bottle">splash water bottles</a>, which deal damage by 1<span class="hidden-alt-text">HP</span><span class="nowrap mc-hearts"><span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="0.5 hearts"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="💔" src="/images/Half_Heart_%28icon%29.png?cb16e" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span></span> per splash water bottle or half-second in water or rain. While in water, they slowly sink while taking damage. Striders still take damage from rain even if they are in lava. However, they are not harmed when standing in a filled <a href="/w/Cauldron" title="Cauldron">cauldron</a> as a baby. They also cannot be harmed by <a href="/w/Snowfall" title="Snowfall">snowfall</a> or <a href="/w/Snowball" title="Snowball">snowballs</a>. They take extra damage from freezing in <a href="/w/Powder_snow" class="mw-redirect" title="Powder snow">powder snow</a>.
</p><p>Unlike <a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">piglins</a> and <a href="/w/Hoglin" title="Hoglin">hoglins</a>, striders can exist safely in the <a href="/w/Overworld" title="Overworld">Overworld</a>, as long as they are kept away from water and rain. Striders outside of lava change to a dull purple color, change their expression to more of a frown, shiver, and their legs become slightly shorter. They also move slower when outside of lava.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> 
</p><p>If a strider has the <span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style="height:18px;width:18px"><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Speed" title="Speed"><img alt="" src="/images/EffectSprite_speed.png?0a273" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="18" height="18" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="18" data-file-height="18"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Speed" title="Speed"><span class="sprite-text">Speed</span></a></span> effect applied to it, it moves faster on both land and lava (though its land speed is still considerably slower). If a zombified piglin is riding a strider, the strider pursues the player if the zombified piglin is angered.
</p><p>Due to a bug,<sup id="cite_ref-StriderLavaBug_8-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-StriderLavaBug-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> striders that fall from a height take fall damage when landing in lava.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>
</p><p>A baby strider on an adult strider still grows into an adult. Apart from this, adult striders riding other adult striders do not spawn naturally. Baby striders not riding on an adult follow the closest adult strider.
</p>
<ul class="gallery mw-gallery-traditional">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Riding">Riding</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Strider?section=5&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Riding" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Strider?action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section's source code: Riding"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Riding" title="Riding">Riding</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Strider_riding.gif" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Strider_riding.gif/300px-Strider_riding.gif?4da40" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/Strider_riding.gif?4da40 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="338"></a><figcaption>A player riding a strider.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The player can ride on an adult strider using a <a href="/w/Saddle" title="Saddle">saddle</a>. 
</p><p>Similar to how <a href="/w/Pig" title="Pig">pigs</a> are controlled using a <a href="/w/Carrot_on_a_stick" class="mw-redirect" title="Carrot on a stick">carrot on a stick</a>, striders move forward automatically while their direction is influenced using a <a href="/w/Warped_fungus_on_a_stick" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus on a stick">warped fungus on a stick</a>, at a speed of 4.24 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / 3.71 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> if on a flat lava surface (such as the Nether <a href="/w/Lava_sea" class="mw-redirect" title="Lava sea">lava sea</a>) or 1.78 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / 1.64 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> if on land. They walk especially slowly against the lava flow direction.
</p><p>When a warped fungus on a stick is <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">used</span>, the strider enters a boost for a random duration between 140 to 980 game ticks (7 to 49 seconds)‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / 320 game ticks (16 seconds)‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>. Each boost takes 1 point of durability from the warped fungus on a stick. If the durability of the warped fungus on a stick reaches 0, it turns into a fishing rod.
</p><p>While boosted, the strider gradually accelerates to its peak speed of 9.12 m/s ‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / 7.98 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> until halfway through the boost, and then decelerates to its default speed by the end of the boost. Specifically, the speed of the strider increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>1.15</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mstyle></mrow></math> times the original speed, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>t</mi></mstyle></mrow></math> is the time already passed since the start of the boost, and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></mstyle></mrow></math> is the total duration of the boost. No matter how many ticks the boost lasts, the average speed of the strider during a full boost cycle is roughly 7.34 m/s ‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / 6.42 m/s‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>.
</p><p>Striders also follow players holding a <a href="/w/Warped_fungus" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus">warped fungus</a> or a warped fungus on a stick. 
</p><p>Unlike underwater <a href="/w/Boat" title="Boat">boats</a>, players riding striders are not dismounted if the strider submerges in lava, and striders rise back up to the surface if this happens. However, players risk getting burned by the lava while submerged. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, players can start riding a strider that is fully submerged in lava.
</p><p>A strider ridden into flowing lava slowly rises to the top. Fall damage does not affect striders that have dropped onto flowing lava, unlike the bug<sup id="cite_ref-StriderLavaBug_8-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-StriderLavaBug-8"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> for lava source blocks. When ridden over land, striders automatically walk up any one block high slope. They also cross any 1-wide block gap or air space that is only one block higher - diagonally up - when ridden directly upward and not completely sideways to the slope.
</p><p>To safely dismount from a strider, a player who does not have <a href="/w/Fire_Resistance" title="Fire Resistance">Fire Resistance</a> may face a solid block within reach before dismounting to dismount onto that block,<sup id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-9"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> instead of at the strider's location (which is usually in lava<sup id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>).‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup><sup id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-11"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A strider can still be equipped with a saddle while another mob is riding it.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Breeding">Breeding</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Strider?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Breeding" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Strider?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Breeding"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Breeding" title="Breeding">Breeding</a></div>
<p>If striders are given <a href="/w/Warped_fungus" class="mw-redirect" title="Warped fungus">warped fungus</a>, they breed to create baby striders, granting the player 1–7 <a href="/w/Experience" title="Experience">experience</a> orbs. The parent striders have a cooldown of about 5 minutes before they can breed again. All babies obtained through breeding take 20 minutes to grow up. The growth of baby striders can be accelerated using warped fungus; each use takes 10% off of the remaining time to grow up.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Trivia">Trivia</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Strider?section=20&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trivia" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Strider?action=edit&section=20" title="Edit section's source code: Trivia"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Strider_fin.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Strider_fin.png/64px-Strider_fin.png?6728d" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="64" height="73" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Strider_fin.png/128px-Strider_fin.png?6728d 2x" data-file-width="450" data-file-height="514"></a><figcaption>Strider's fin</figcaption></figure>
<ul><li>Striders previously had a fin in their texture file. The fin was not visible in-game and was removed in 20w15a.</li>
<li>If commands are used to saddle a baby strider, and the player rides the baby strider in lava, the player takes fire damage due to not being high enough to avoid the lava.</li>
<li>Mojang added striders to the game as the solution to the community request for lava boats.<sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Prior to this, actual <a href="/w/Obsidian_Boat" title="Obsidian Boat">lava boats</a> made of <a href="/w/Obsidian" title="Obsidian">obsidian</a> were briefly added as an April Fools prank.</li>
<li>At one point in the strider's development, before it was added to the game, a strider out of lava would retract its legs and start to take damage while bouncing around until it died, similar to how <a href="/w/Fish" title="Fish">fish</a> suffocate when out of water. This feature was discarded for being "kind of sad".<sup id="cite_ref-meet_strider_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-meet_strider-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Striders were planned to have their own unique armor and saddle, but this was decided against.<sup id="cite_ref-MCIA_kingbdogz_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MCIA_kingbdogz-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Striders were initially going to have a long tongue with which they could eat things, similar to <a href="/w/Frog" title="Frog">frogs</a>. The different items would all have various effects, such as <a href="/w/Sword" title="Sword">swords</a> hurting the strider, and <a href="/w/TNT" title="TNT">TNT</a> exploding.<sup id="cite_ref-MCIA_kingbdogz_18-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MCIA_kingbdogz-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Part of the reason that striders drop string (from their bristles) was to answer the question of "how do <a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">piglins</a> make crossbows?".<sup id="cite_ref-meet_strider_17-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-meet_strider-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In <i><a href="/w/Legends:Return_of_the_Piglins" title="Legends:Return of the Piglins">Minecraft Legends: Return of the Piglins</a></i>, striders shed the strings that piglins used to make crossbows.<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>The bobbing animation that the strider makes while walking was initially an accident. However, the developers thought it was "quirky and fun", so it was added as a feature.<sup id="cite_ref-meet_strider_17-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-meet_strider-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>Internally the strider was originally referred to as the <code>derp-a-tron</code>.<sup id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>In a video summarizing the <a href="/w/Tiny_Takeover" title="Tiny Takeover">Tiny Takeover</a> drop, Mojang developer <a href="/w/Slicedlime" title="Slicedlime">Slicedlime</a> refers to baby Striders as "Striderlings" before adding that he made up this word.<sup id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li></ul>
